LOG1_DD: I joined 1.5°C as an intern and had to step into the CTO role ten months later, when the founding engineer left. As co-founder and CTO, I lead the computer vision, satellite imagery, and fire-risk models — with the engineering, ML, and environmental science team that builds them with me.
LOG2_DD: Nine AI agents in production on Hermes, open-source, on our own servers. They support different areas of the company, like engineering, sales, support, marketing, and fire alerts, and each one has a person accountable for it.
LOG_DELEGATION_DD: I took on Customer Success, Support, and Marketing at different points and led HR for two years. I organized support ticketing and CS documentation, covered Marketing between hires, and handed each area off.
LOG3_DD: Contributor since 2022 to ForeFire, CNRS's open-source wildfire simulator, maintainer since 2025, and co-author on its JOSS paper — reviewing and merging PRs, cutting releases, Dockerization, CI/CD, documentation.
LOG4_DD: Open to senior technical leadership or senior individual contributor roles in climate, energy, govtech, and open source — where the hard part isn't the model but putting it inside an operation where being wrong is expensive.
PANTERA_ALT: Wildfire smoke rising over farmland, detected and boxed by the Pantera camera network.
PANTERA_BODY: The wildfire AI platform I lead end to end at 1.5°C — field cameras, satellite imagery, and fire-risk models in one operation.

FOREFIRE_BODY: The open-source fire-spread simulator built by CNRS. I maintain it outside the day job and co-authored its JOSS paper.
ABOUT_MUSIC: Ten years of formal piano, self-taught guitar, and saxophone in a Carnaval bloco — where I built the group's sheet music player.
ABOUT_PROJECTS: A side habit of turning public data into tools: an interactive map of Brazil's power grid (brasil-grid) and an open-data tracker for Congress (fichadopolitico).
CONTACT_BODY: If you're building something ambitious in AI, climate, or public-interest tech, write to me. I'd like to hear about it.
